text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher across the board in quiet dealings. July and September added $35 to close at $1,830 and $1,850 per tonne respectively. Weather in Brazil's coffee areas is forecast to be mild and private US forecaster Weather Services Corporation said a warm ridge of high pressure dominating Brazil's coffee belt is expected to continue for the next seven days.

Arabica futures in New York ended higher and toward the day's peaks, bolstered by a late session round of trade and local buying. July added 2.00 cents/lb to close at 200.00 cents/lb, while September was up by 5.05 cents/lb at 180.15 cents/lb. Traders said spread action continues to suggest there is something behind the scenes with possibly some increased roaster interest based on the switches. It was added there could be renewed concerns about tightness as the period of heavy shipments is over and it will take several months before new crop coffee comes onto the market. Hence, it is expected, that prices will rise again. An indication for the expected tightness is that exchange-certified coffee stocks are on the decline and that therefore supplies could become very tight again in the August/October period ahead of the harvest of many new-crop coffees.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 248 bags on June 24 to 45,927 bags from 46,175 bags the previous day and 46,425 bags on June 20. There were 10,387 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

FINLAND ** - Finland imported 119,876 bags of coffee in March 1997, significantly up on the 77,157 bags imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 289,300 bags, 45 percent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 48 percent to 1.120 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Brazil (77,100 vs 36,900 bags) and Colombia (70,400 vs 65,500 bags).
The country exported 45,300 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, 44 percent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 78 percent to 173,000 bags.

UNITED KINGDOM ** - The UK imported 272,089 bags of coffee in March 1997, 9 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 787,700 bags, roughly the same what was imported in January/March 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 12 percent to 3.114 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Uganda (68,400 vs 24,200 bags), Colombia (65,600 vs 62,700 bags), Indonesia (68,800 vs 57,800 bags) and Vietnam (113,700 vs 112,800 bags).
The country exported 125,500 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, 13 percent less than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 0.8 percent to 542,600 bags.
